# Conformance summary: after Jobs 1-3 (report-side visibility)

Generated by hand against the nine goldens regenerated by
`FOREVER_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test --tags=with_db ./sim/conformance/...`
on top of `sim/conformance`'s talent-free rework (every preset now
builds with an empty talent string; talent-only abilities moved to each
golden's own "Talent-gated spells" section). All counts below are at
level 60, the level every preset reaches, so a spell that is only
registered below 60 is not represented in these totals (see each
golden's own full level ladder - 10/20/30/38/40/50/60 - for those).

"Before" is the committed golden on `forever` before this rework (full
real talent builds); "after Job 1" is the state this file originally
documented, once talent burial was removed but before the report-side
fixes below; "after Jobs 1-3" is the current golden. Compare with care:
"before" buried every talent-modifier row as a mismatch
(Frostbolt/Earth Shock/Starfire's talent-reduced cost, Wrath's
talent-reduced cast time, etc.), so a drop in mismatch count from before
to "after Job 1" is mostly that burial being removed, not fixes
landing. The drop from "after Job 1" to "after Jobs 1-3" below IS real
report-side fixes landing - no engine code changed in this lane; every
number that moved was always true of the engine, this report just
could not see it before:

- **Job 1** widened `engineDuration` (`sim/conformance/compare.go`) to
  search every aura already registered on the caster, the caster's
  current target, and any Pet the caster's Character owns - not just
  `RelatedSelfBuff`/`Dot(target)` - matched by `ActionID.SpellID`
  against every rank spellconst's client table lists under the same
  name (`siblingSpellIDs`), since several of the engine's own aura
  helpers (totem buffs among them) pin one shared aura to a single
  fixed rank's SpellID regardless of which rank actually cast it. A row
  that still reads `duration_ms X->0` now also says
  `(no aura registered)` when nothing was found anywhere this function
  looked, distinguishing a real "not implemented as a trackable aura at
  all" (a trap's armed lifetime) from the old blind zero. See
  `compare.go`'s `engineDuration` doc comment for the full search order
  and `sim/conformance/compare_test.go` for the fake-spell-and-aura unit
  tests covering it (caster aura, target aura, pet aura, sibling-rank
  matching, and the "nothing found anywhere" case).

  One build-specific wrinkle this surfaced: Strength of Earth Totem and
  Grace of Air Totem's buff auras are the SAME `*core.Aura` object this
  report's standard build's `core.FullBuffs.Player` already applies as
  a permanent external raid buff (`core.MakePermanent` in
  `sim/core/buffs.go`, mutating `aura.Duration` to `core.NeverExpires`
  in place). Every preset here builds with full buffs, so by the time
  the totem's own cast would activate that aura, it is already
  permanent - this report now reports it as such (engine duration
  `-1`, the client's own "until removed" sentinel, not a defect) rather
  than the old blind `0`. This is a fact about the comparison's build
  configuration, not about the totem spell's own registration; it is
  called out per-row below rather than papered over.

  A second wrinkle this fixed outright: a proc-style aura with no
  natural timeout (Priest's Inner Focus, Shadowform) carries
  `core.NeverExpires` too. The very first version of this widened
  search truncated that `math.MaxInt64`-nanosecond value into an int32
  millisecond count and reported garbage (`2077252342`); `compare.go`
  now has a dedicated `auraDurationMS` that reads `NeverExpires` as the
  client's own `-1` sentinel, and `verdictFor` accepts an engine `-1` as
  matching a client `-1` (previously only an engine `0` could match a
  client `-1`, the "never found anything" case this report used to be
  stuck with). Inner Focus now reads `match`; Shadowform's duration
  stops contributing to its mismatch (it still mismatches on
  `cooldown_ms`/`gcd_ms`, a real, separate registration gap).

- **Job 2** answers, rather than flags, the "percent-of-mana cost vs.
  flat client column" question - see the rewritten vocabulary bullet
  below. No code changed for this job: `sim/core/spellconst` cannot
  carry a field the generated `data/builds/<build>/spellconst/*.json`
  files do not emit (that pipeline lives in the `forever` repo, out of
  this lane's scope), so the answer lives in `compare.go`'s doc comment
  and here.

- **Job 3** drops the client's generic "Attack" entry - the basic
  melee-swing button, not a player-cast spell, reused across many
  contexts and sometimes id-colliding with a real engine spell (shaman's
  Searing Totem's own instant attack sub-spell shares its ids) - from
  the comparison entirely (`rowFor` in `compare.go`). It no longer
  appears in any class's golden, spells table or required-level table.

Every column is match/mismatch at level 60 combining the Spells and
Talent-gated tables. Warrior's drop in matches (13->7) is NOT a
regression: Job 1's wider search found real, previously-invisible
engine durations for several warrior self-buffs that disagree with the
client's number (a genuine stale-literal or registration gap, now
visible instead of hidden behind a blind `missing aura duration` zero),
which correctly reclassifies them from "no data to compare" into
"compared, and wrong." Priest and Druid are unchanged at level 60
specifically (their remaining mismatches are registration gaps and
percent-costs, not duration visibility, so Job 1 had nothing to find
for those two at this level - see each section). Shaman's huge
mismatch count is almost entirely one systemic cause (every totem's
GCD, see below), not 232 independent defects - see the shaman section's
lead note.

## Likely-cause vocabulary

Every mismatch below is tagged with one of:

- **stale vanilla literal** - the engine still carries an old
  pre-Forever Classic number (cost, cast time, cooldown, or dot
  duration) that Forever's spellconst build changed and the engine's
  source was never updated to match.
- **missing aura duration** - the client names a nonzero duration and
  `engineDuration` (`compare.go`) found no aura or Dot anywhere it
  looked: `RelatedSelfBuff`, `Dot(target)`, every aura already
  registered on the caster, on the caster's current target, or on any
  Pet the caster's Character owns (Job 1 widened this from just the
  first two). A row in this state now also says
  `(no aura registered)` in its Diff text. What is left in this bucket
  after Job 1 is the real remainder: a trap's armed lifetime before it
  triggers (Explosive/Freezing Trap, Strider Kick), and a handful of
  self-buffs with no trackable aura under any name this report can
  find (Wing Clip, Stoneskin/Tremor/Windfury/Windwall/Mana Spring
  Totem). A row that instead shows a real, nonzero engine number -
  found, but disagreeing with the client - is a **stale vanilla
  literal** or **semantic mismatch** now, not this tag.
- **percent-of-mana cost vs. flat client column - answered** -
  confirmed against build 1.60.1.70009's raw `SpellPower.csv`: every
  spell whose spellconst `cost` reads a flat 0 while the engine spends
  a fraction of base mana (Hunter's Bestial Wrath 12%, Multi-Shot
  13.9%; Warlock's four summons, 80-100%; Druid's Cat Form 55%, Moonkin
  Form 35%, Innervate 5%) has a real, nonzero `PowerCostPct` column in
  that raw table, matching the engine's percent almost exactly - these
  are correct engine behavior this report could not previously verify,
  not stale formulas. **2026-10-07 update:** the pipeline now emits
  `cost_pct`, `spellconst.Spell` carries it as `CostPct`, and the cost
  column compares it as that share of the preset's base mana (printed
  as e.g. `181.95 (15% base mana)`). The first run with it in place
  found six engine spells registered FREE that the client prices this
  way - Arcane Blast 15% (plus its +175%-per-stack ramp, which a free
  spell could never have carried), Judgement 6% (a 2026-10-06
  "conformance fix" had removed the cost on the strength of the flat
  zero), Shadowform 40%, Divine Favor 4%, Bane of Havoc 5%, Strider
  Kick 5.81% - all fixed the same day; every percent-priced row the
  engine registers now matches. Two exceptions this check also found,
  real defects rather than visibility gaps, for their own class lanes:
  **Warlock's Summon Imp** shares Felhunter/Voidwalker/Succubus's
  100%-of-base-mana cost variable (`sim/warlock/summon_demon.go`)
  instead of its own real 80% (`PowerCostPct` 80 vs. 100); **Shaman's
  Stormstrike** is NOT a percent-cost spell at all in the client
  (`PowerCostPct` 0, flat `ManaCost` 125, matching spellconst's cost
  column already) - `sim/shaman/stormstrike.go`'s
  `ManaCost.BaseCost: .21` treats it as 21%-of-base-mana anyway, a
  stale vanilla-era literal. See `compare.go`'s doc comment above
  `clientCostTypeName` for the full per-spell numbers checked.
- **registration gap** - the spell's own `SpellConfig` simply never
  sets the field in question (no `RequiredLevel`, no `Cost`, no `CD`),
  so the engine's default zero-value is read as a mismatch rather than
  a missing number.
- **semantic mismatch** - both sides have a real, correct number, but
  they are not measuring the same thing (a trap's total armed lifetime
  versus its damage-tick length; Rogue's Slice and Dice base 6s versus
  the combo-point-scaled duration the engine's aura actually carries).
- **not a real spell** - the client's class table carries an entry
  (the generic melee "Attack" button) that was never meant to be an
  engine-registered spell at all. As of Job 3 this is no longer a
  mismatch tag to apply by hand: `rowFor` drops every row named
  "Attack" before it reaches comparison, so it cannot appear in any
  golden below.
- **full-buffs duration artifact** (new) - the engine aura
  `engineDuration` found is the exact same object this report's build
  already activated permanently via `core.FullBuffs.Player` or
  `core.FullBuffs.Debuffs` (`core.MakePermanent`, which mutates
  `aura.Duration` to `core.NeverExpires` in place), so its duration
  reads the client's own `-1` sentinel - true of this report's standard
  build, not a claim about the spell's own registered duration. Seen on
  a caster self-buff (Strength of Earth Totem, Grace of Air Totem - see
  the shaman section) and a target debuff alike (Warlock's Curse of
  Recklessness rank 4).

## Required-level mismatches (registration gaps, not numbers)

the client's `spell_level` places above 1, i.e. the spell's own
`SpellConfig` never sets `RequiredLevel`. One exception is called out
separately. This is a work list, not a numeric target - the fix in
every row is "add `RequiredLevel: <client value>` to this spell's

Vampiric Embrace's duration is newly VISIBLE but not newly correct: Job

before, and it still disagrees with the client's 30000ms (a stale
vanilla literal shape, not a registration gap as this bucket
previously assumed).

| Spell | Field | Client | Engine | Likely cause |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Shadowform | cooldown_ms, gcd_ms | 1500 / 1500 | 0 / 0 | registration gap - Shadowform looks implemented as a toggle/aura without the normal cast wrapper the client models (no `CD`, no `GCD`) |
| Vampiric Embrace | cooldown_ms, duration_ms, required_level | 60000 / 30000 / 30 | 0 / 60000 / 0 | registration gap (cooldown, required level); duration is a real engine number (newly visible by Job 1) that is 2x the client's, a stale-literal shape worth the priest lane's own look |

This is still the cleanest class after Jobs 1-3 - only 2 mismatches at
level 60, both on one talent-gated spell plus Shadowform's missing
cast wrapper.

### Shaman

Shaman's count is still dominated by one systemic defect repeated
across every totem - the GCD (every totem's `gcd_ms` is 1000 on the
client, 1500 in the engine) - not 232 independent defects. Job 3
dropped the client's "Attack" entry (which, for shaman specifically,
collided with Searing Totem's own instant attack sub-spell's SpellID)
out of the comparison entirely; it no longer appears anywhere in this
golden, including the required-level table above. Job 1's wider search
resolved every totem's duration one of three ways, and no totem's
*duration* is a "missing aura" anymore - each is now one of:

- **Found and now matches**: Magma Totem and Searing Totem's own
  (already-correct) durations stop contributing to their mismatch -
  only `gcd_ms` remains for them.
- **Found, a real-but-different number**: Healing Stream Totem's buff
  aura is a real, finite 60000ms, not the client's 300000 - a genuine
  stale-literal-shaped disagreement to confirm, not a visibility gap.
- **Found, but a full-buffs artifact**: Strength of Earth Totem and
  Grace of Air Totem's buff auras are the exact same `*core.Aura`
  object `core.FullBuffs.Player` already activates permanently in this
  report's standard build (`core.MakePermanent` - see the vocabulary
  entry above), so they read `-1` rather than a real cast-produced
  timer. This is a fact about the build, not the totem spells'
  registration.
- **Still not found at all**: Stoneskin, Tremor, Windfury, Windwall and
  Mana Spring Totem's buffs still have no trackable aura under any name
  this report can find (Windfury's own buff aura, for one, carries no
  `ActionID` at all, so it could never match regardless of search
  breadth) - genuinely still **missing aura duration**, now flagged
  `(no aura registered)` in their Diff text.

| Spell | Field | Client | Engine | Likely cause |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Every totem (all ranks) | gcd_ms | 1000 | 1500 | stale vanilla literal - the engine still gives every totem the standard 1.5s GCD; Forever's client gives totems a 1s GCD and the engine was never updated for this class of spell |
| Strength of Earth Totem, Grace of Air Totem (all ranks) | duration_ms | 300000 | -1 | full-buffs duration artifact (see vocabulary) |
| Healing Stream Totem (all ranks) | duration_ms | 300000 | 60000 | newly visible by Job 1 - a real, finite engine duration that simply disagrees with the client's, likely a stale literal |
| Stoneskin Totem, Tremor Totem, Windfury Totem, Windwall Totem, Mana Spring Totem (all ranks) | duration_ms | 300000 | 0 (no aura registered) | missing aura duration - still true after Job 1's wider search |
| Lightning Bolt ranks 4-10 | cost, cast_time_ms | 60.00-220.00 / 2500 | 75.00-265.00 / 3000 | stale vanilla literal - ranks 1-3 already match; ranks 4+ are still on the old Classic cast time (3000ms) and cost table instead of Forever's (2500ms) |
| Chain Lightning (all ranks) | cost, cast_time_ms | 225.00-485.00 / 2000 | 280.00-605.00 / 2500 | stale vanilla literal, same shape as Lightning Bolt |
| Stormstrike (talent-gated) | cost, cooldown_ms | 125.00 / 8000 | 319.20 / 20000 | cost is a stale vanilla literal, NOT percent-of-mana visibility: the client's raw `SpellPower.csv` row for Stormstrike has `PowerCostPct` 0 and a real flat `ManaCost` of 125 (matching spellconst's own cost column already) - `sim/shaman/stormstrike.go`'s `ManaCost.BaseCost: .21` treats it as 21%-of-base-mana anyway. Cooldown is also a stale vanilla literal (20s was live Classic's cooldown; Forever's client shortened it to 8s). Job 1 confirmed the DURATION side of this spell outright (12000=12000, no longer in its Diff). |
| Water Shield (talent-gated) | cooldown_ms | 15000 | 0 | registration gap - no `CD` configured (Job 1 confirmed its duration outright, 600000=600000, no longer in its Diff) |
| Rage of the Farseer (talent-gated) | gcd_ms | 0 | 1500 | registration gap - a cooldown-only talent ability the client flags GCD-less, same shape as Warlock's Bane of Havoc |

### Rogue

Job 1 confirmed Adrenaline Rush and Ghostly Strike's durations outright
(both now full `match` rows) and Blade Flurry's (now mismatching only
on `required_level`). It also found real, previously-invisible engine
auras for Riposte (5000ms vs. the client's 6000 - a real, small
disagreement) and Expose Armor (a `core.FullBuffs.Debuffs` artifact,
`-1`, same shape as Warlock's Curse of Recklessness above). Only
Hemorrhage and Premeditation are still genuinely **missing aura
duration**; Rupture still reads `0` too, but without
`(no aura registered)` - something on its target is returning a real,
zero-length Dot/aura rather than nothing at all, alongside the same
"bogus zero-valued extra row" shape (`required_level` also reads 0)
seen on Hunter's Raptor Strike and Druid's Rip - worth the rogue lane's
own look rather than this report's.

| Spell | Field | Client | Engine | Likely cause |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Stealth | cooldown_ms | 10000 | 0 | registration gap - no `CD` configured |
| Expose Armor | duration_ms | 30000 | -1 | full-buffs duration artifact (see vocabulary) |
| Riposte | duration_ms | 6000 | 5000 | newly visible by Job 1 - a real, nonzero engine duration that simply disagrees with the client's |
| Hemorrhage, Premeditation | duration_ms | 15000 / 20000 | 0 (no aura registered) | missing aura duration - still true after Job 1's wider search |
| Rupture | duration_ms, required_level | 6000 / 60 | 0 / 0 | engine reads a real but zero-length duration (no `(no aura registered)` note), likely the same bogus-extra-row shape as Hunter's Raptor Strike and Druid's Rip - worth the rogue lane's own look |
| Slice and Dice | duration_ms, required_level | 6000 / 42 | 21000 / 0 | semantic mismatch, newly visible by Job 1: the engine's aura is real (21000ms, not found before) but is the combo-point-scaled duration, not the client's base 6s - a real but different number, same shape as Immolation Trap above |

Rogue has the fewest matches of any class (5 combining both tables at
level 60) but also the fewest distinct defects - most of what remains
is one of two systemic causes (missing aura duration and Stealth's
missing cooldown), not 26 independent numeric bugs. CombatSwordsRogue's
pre-existing WeaponExpertise talent-rewrite panic (sim/rogue/talents.go,
tracked separately) does not affect this report: it only panicked under
that preset's real 5-point talent spend, and the empty-talent
comparison build never reaches that code path.

## Job 2: the percent-of-mana cost question, answered

The open question this file used to leave for a follow-up lane is
answered, not just flagged. Checked directly against build
1.60.1.70009's raw `SpellPower.csv` (`data/builds/1.60.1.70009/raw/`
in the `forever` repo), which has its own `PowerCostPct` column that
`spellconst`'s generated JSON never carries (its pipeline reads
`SpellPower.csv`'s flat `ManaCost` column only):

| Spell | Client `PowerCostPct` | Engine `ManaCostOptions.BaseCost` |
|---|---|---|
| Hunter Bestial Wrath (19574) | 12% | 0.12 |
| Hunter Multi-Shot (2643) | 13.9% | 0.139 |
| Warlock Summon Felhunter (691) | 100% | 1.0 |
| Warlock Summon Voidwalker (697) | 100% | 1.0 |
| Warlock Summon Succubus (712) | 100% | 1.0 |
| Warlock Summon Imp (688) | 80% | 1.0 (bug - see the warlock section) |
| Druid Cat Form (768) | 55% | 0.55 |
| Druid Moonkin Form (24858) | 35% | 0.35 |
| Druid Innervate (29166) | 5% | 0.05 |

Every one of these (Summon Imp aside) is the engine's percent model
matching the client's real percent-cost field exactly - correct engine
behavior this report could not previously verify, not a stale formula.
The fix that would surface this directly in the golden tables above,
rather than in this file and `compare.go`'s doc comment, is extending
the `forever` repo's data pipeline to emit `PowerCostPct` into
`spellconst`'s generated JSON and `spellconst.Spell` to carry it, so
`verdictFor` could compare percent-to-percent - out of this lane's
`sim/conformance`/`sim/core/spellconst` scope, since that pipeline
lives in a different repository.

Shaman's Stormstrike is explicitly NOT one of these: its raw
`SpellPower.csv` row has `PowerCostPct` 0 and a real flat `ManaCost` of
125, matching spellconst's own cost column already - its mismatch is a
stale vanilla-era literal in `sim/shaman/stormstrike.go`, not a
visibility gap (see the shaman section above).
